newsitem.title: UK: ATHLETICS-JARRETT INFLICTS ANOTHER DEFEAT ON JACKSON.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-JARRETT INFLICTS ANOTHER DEFEAT ON JACKSON.

text.p: Tony Jarrett scored what could prove to be a significant victory over his old rival Colin Jackson when he won the British 110 metres hurdles title at the world championship trials on Saturday.
Jarrett, 28, who has so often trailed home in 30-year-old Jackson's footsteps, led him across the line in 13.33 seconds with the world record holder second in 13.39.

The two guaranteed themselves their places in Britain's team for the world championships in Athens next month, but Jarrett, who has noe beaten Jarrett three times this season, clearly had more to be pleased about than Jackson, currently ranked only 20th in the world.
"He got a good start as he usually does," said Jarrett, "But I just kept him in my sights and reeled him in. I couldn't have done that a few years ago."
While Jarrett was pleased with his performance, sprinter Ian Mackie was delighted with his.
Mackie took over Linford Christie's 100 metres title in the absence of the 37-year-old grandfather who was not running in this meeting for the first time since the early 1980s.
Mackie, from Scotland, won in convincing style, clocking 10.28 seconds with Darren Campbell second in 10.29.
"I'm looking forward to Athens and my goal is to get to the final there," he said, "then to finish as high up in the final as I can."

Owain Chambers was third in 10.42 while Jason Livingston, hoping for a a place in Athens following his return from a drugs ban imposed at the 1992 Olympics, looks set to miss out after finishing fourth in 10.43.
The seemingly-ageless Tessa Sanderson, now 41, looks set to go to Athens 23 years after first appearing in a major competition -- the 1974 European Championships.
Sanderson, who competed at her sixth Olympics last summer, won the javelin with a throw of 58.30m having achieved the qualifying standard last year.
Earlier Kelly Holmes won the 800 metres and said she would double up at 800 and 1500 metres at the worlds.
"The focus will be the 1500, but I most probably will enter the 800 if I am selected," said Holmes.
"But until I've finished the 1500m final I won't even consider the 800."

Holmes, 27, an army sergeant until she quits the military life in October, hit the front 250 metres from the line after tucking in behind Hayley Parry for the first lap. She eventually sprinted clear to win in one minute 58.69 seconds, her eighth win of the season.
Sally Gunnell, the former Olympic and World 400 metres hurdles champion, cruised into Sunday's 400 hurdles final with an effortless and undemanding victory in 55.71 seconds.
She showed a vast improvement over last week's run in Oslo when she trailed in fifth in 55.53 seconds, more than two seconds behind winner Deon Hemmings.
